items.headline: Dow hits a one-month high while the Nasdaq ends flat
items.note: On Tuesday the Dow rose 1.02% to 52,495.88, the S&P 500 gained about 0.3% and the Nasdaq slipped 0.02%. Healthcare, financials and utilities led, while tech lagged, so the rally was not driven by big tech.

items.headline: Netflix posts Q3 profit jump, guides to a lower Q4 margin
items.note: Revenue was $12.87B (up 12%), operating margin 34.6% and EPS $0.87 vs $0.59 a year ago. It guided Q4 operating margin to 26%, including about 120 basis points from recent headcount cuts. I couldn't confirm how the stock reacted.

items.headline: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a public-benefit fund
items.note: The commitment needs stockholder approval, and the fund can't be used for lobbying or political giving. It adds to earlier pledges, so roughly 20% of shares would go to the public good.

items.headline: OpenAI's Altman says the company will build a humanoid robot
items.note: He expects a demo in 2027 and OpenAI lists 27 robotics openings, including hardware roles. Robotics is becoming a hiring area at the big labs.

items.headline: Disney hires most of Character.AI's staff after its bankruptcy filing
items.note: Disney offered jobs to at least 60 employees, most of whom accepted, and has a $20 million stalking-horse bid for assets, so a higher bid is still possible. Struggling AI startups are being absorbed by large companies.

items.headline: Reflection AI releases open-weight Beam under Apache 2.0
items.note: Beam has 501B total and 23B active parameters. It scores 80.1% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 by Reflection's own table, below top Chinese models, but uses far fewer tokens per attempt. Its weights are free to download and test.

items.headline: US cybersecurity postings fall 26%, but AI security roles surge
items.note: CyberSN counted 235,786 postings in Jan–Sep 2026, a four-year low. AI Security Engineer demand rose 268.3% and Cyber Data Scientist 203.5%, so data skills plus security are in demand.

learn.explain: Revenue is all the money a company brings in from sales. Profit is what's left after subtracting costs. Margin is profit as a percentage of revenue, which shows how much of each dollar the company keeps. In its Q3 report, Netflix had $12.87B of revenue and a 34.6% operating margin, so it kept about 35 cents of each dollar before interest and taxes. It guided next quarter's margin down to 26%, partly because of costs tied to headcount cuts. A company can grow revenue and still look worse if its margin shrinks.
learn.try: Open Netflix's Q3 shareholder letter, find operating income, and divide it by revenue to check the margin.
